title: Session watermark finality and rate-limit reconciliation for streaming metering
creator: Ava Chen
description: Production streams occasionally produce final token charges that are later rolled back or duplicated when rate-limit backpressure and client reconnects interact with our provisional-crediting path. Root cause appears to be a mismatch between the session-level watermark (what we consider "finalized" for metering) and the rate-limiter's hold/release semantics for multiplexed connections. This causes customers to see transient overcharges followed by retroactive credits, which undermines trust and increases support load.
reproduction_steps: Open a long-lived multiplexed websocket session with 3 concurrent streams using the streaming API
Trigger a burst: send a large prompt that causes server-side batching and a short-lived rate-limit enforcement window
Simulate a network blip causing client reconnect that resumes the same session id and replays pending chunks
Observe token ledger entries: duplicate finalization events, provisional credits not reconciled until a delayed backfill task runs
impact: High: affects billing accuracy for long-running streaming sessions under bursty traffic. Several enterprise customers reported unexpected credit adjustments and opened support tickets. Financial exposure is bounded but reputational impact is material.
proposal_summary: Introduce a deterministic session-finality watermarking algorithm plus a rate-limit-aware checkpoint handshake so that token finalization only occurs when both: (a) the session watermark advances past the fragment, and (b) the rate-limiter has acknowledged the request as committed (or the session is explicitly tombstoned). Add a telemetry counter for provisional vs finalized credits and a short-term backfill job to reconcile existing drift.
acceptance_criteria: Session_finalized_watermark metric accurately monotonically advances per-session; no final token entry is emitted for a fragment until watermark and rate-limiter commit signals are observed
Idempotency key semantics preserved across reconnects: replayed fragments do not create duplicate finalized charges
New dashboard shows provisional_credit_count and final_credit_count per session and alerts when provisional > final for > 5m
Backfill reconciler runs and reduces number of outstanding provisional credits for impacted sessions by >= 90% in staging
Automated e2e test that simulates reconnect+burst verifies no duplicate final charges
design_notes: Use a lightweight vector-clock-like watermark per session: (last_committed_offset, last_seen_offset, tombstone_flag). This avoids cross-session global locks and keeps memory bounded.
Rate-limiter will emit a commit token (rate_commit_id) when a request is accepted from the queue; metering will join on rate_commit_id before emitting final ledger rows.

To avoid latency regressions we will allow provisional credits to be shown to the console immediately but mark them as provisional; finalization path must be idempotent and cheap (single conditional write with compare-and-swap on session watermark).
Backfill job will scan sessions with provisional credits older than 2 minutes and attempt deterministic reconciliation using delivery receipts and stored fragment hashes.
implementation_tasks: Add session_watermark data structure to session store and expose atomic CAS endpoint (ENG-403218-1)
Instrument rate-limiter to emit rate_commit_id on accept and wire into metering pipeline (ENG-403218-2)
Introduce provisional_credit flag on ledger rows and a background reconciler that attempts commit -> finalize transitions (ENG-403218-3)
Add e2e test harness that simulates multiplexed reconnects with replay and verifies final ledger state (ENG-403218-4)
Update console to surface provisional vs finalized credits and add an alert rule (ENG-403218-5)
test_plan: Unit tests for watermark CAS semantics including concurrent increments and tombstone behavior
Integration tests: simulate client reconnects, replayed fragments, and rate-limiter-induced holds; assert no duplicate final ledger rows
Load test: verify no more than 2% latency regression on median request path with watermark checks enabled
Staging backfill run on snapshot of impacted sessions and verification against ground-truth from logs
rollout_plan: Feature-flag the new finalization join; default false
Deploy watermark/CAS endpoint and rate-limiter commit emitter to canary cluster; run synthetic reconnect tests
Enable feature flag for 5% of streaming traffic with monitoring of provisional>final delta and error rates
If stable for 48h, ramp to 50% then 100% and schedule backfill run during a low-traffic window
Post-rollout: run reconciliation audits and communicate adjustments to billing/support as needed
